questions: Can we reverse edges multiple times, or is there a limit (e.g., only once per step)?
Does reversing edges flip all edges globally, or only edges incident to the current vertex?
After reversing edges, do subsequent moves use the new edge directions until another reversal?
Is the cost X incurred each time we reverse edges, regardless of whether the graph state repeats?
Can we move along an edge and reverse edges in the same operation step, or must we choose exactly one per step?
Is the goal to minimize total cost, or is there a deterministic procedure implied?
Do we stop immediately upon reaching vertex N, or must we complete the operation that caused arrival?
Are self-loops (u_i = v_i) allowed, and if so, how are they treated in reversal?
